summary: Conformance interface a transactional email provider implements to be independently tested by SOFtruth. Two endpoints. The provider proxies them to its own product; SOFtruth never learns the provider's internal API.
principles: Every assertion is decided by code comparing observed facts, never by a model reading vendor-controlled content.
Concrete test inputs are generated from a per-run seed. The seed is published with the result, so any run is reproducible and no vendor can pre-arrange for fixed inputs.
A failure of SOFtruth's own harness is never recorded as a product failure. See inconclusiveWhen on each assertion.
Delivery is verified against a mailbox SOFtruth controls, not against the provider's own claim of delivery.

send.auth: Provider-issued bearer token, supplied to SOFtruth at onboarding and sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

request.to: string (email address generated by SOFtruth, unique per case)
request.subject: string (seeded random, unique per case)
request.text: string (seeded random body, contains a nonce)
request.idempotencyKey: string (uuid, stable across retries of the same case)

body.messageId: string, opaque, stable, resolvable via the status endpoint

body.state: one of: queued | sent | delivered | bounced | failed

assertions.title: Accepts a well-formed send
assertions.measures: The provider returns 202 with a messageId for a valid request.
assertions.failWhen: Any 4xx/5xx, or 202 with no usable messageId.
assertions.inconclusiveWhen: Network error, timeout, 429, or 5xx that resolves on a later run.

assertions.title: Rejects a malformed send instead of silently accepting
assertions.measures: A request with a missing required field is refused.
assertions.failWhen: HTTP 2xx (silently accepting invalid input) or 5xx (crashing on it).

assertions.title: The message actually arrives
assertions.measures: The exact seeded nonce appears in a mailbox SOFtruth controls, within the delivery window.
assertions.passWhen: A message containing the nonce is received within deliveryWindowSeconds.
assertions.failWhen: No message containing the nonce within the window, and the provider reported state=delivered or state=sent.
assertions.inconclusiveWhen: SOFtruth's own inbox was unreachable during the window, or the provider reported state=queued for the whole window.
assertions.note: This is the assertion the whole product exists for: verified against our mailbox, not against the provider's claim.

assertions.title: Time from accept to arrival
assertions.measures: Seconds between the 202 response and the nonce appearing in our mailbox.
assertions.passWhen: Recorded. This assertion reports a number rather than a verdict; the number is published.
assertions.failWhen: Never fails on its own. Depends on delivery.arrives.

assertions.title: The provider's own status reflects what actually happened
assertions.measures: Provider state versus what SOFtruth observed in its mailbox.
assertions.passWhen: Provider reports delivered AND the nonce arrived; or reports bounced/failed AND it did not arrive.
assertions.failWhen: Provider reports delivered but nothing arrived, or reports failed/bounced but it did arrive.
assertions.inconclusiveWhen: The status endpoint errored, or the message was still queued at the end of the window.
assertions.note: Catches the specific and common case of a provider optimistically reporting delivery it cannot actually confirm.

assertions.title: A hard bounce is reported as a bounce
assertions.measures: Sending to an address guaranteed to bounce produces state=bounced.
assertions.failWhen: State becomes delivered, or remains sent/queued past the window.
assertions.inconclusiveWhen: The status endpoint errored during the window.

runPolicy.note: Every result runs 3 times and the published record shows the ratio (3/3, 2/3). A single run is an anecdote.

openQuestions: Inbox infrastructure for delivery.arrives is not yet chosen. Options: own domain with catch-all plus IMAP polling, or a testing-inbox service with an API. This blocks delivery.arrives, delivery.latency and status.matches-reality.
The guaranteed-bounce address for bounce.reported must be one every provider treats as a hard bounce. A subdomain of a domain SOFtruth controls with a null MX is the likely answer.
Webhook assertions are deliberately out of v1. They would require the provider to call back into SOFtruth, which roughly doubles the integration burden for a vendor's first implementation.
